turns.user: my dumbbells only go up to 24kg each and bench is getting easy, should I just go to 40kg
turns.reply:
At 24kg per hand, you're looking at 48kg total load, so jumping straight to 40kg per hand—which is 80kg total—is a massive leap. That's nearly doubling the weight, and since you're working with dumbbells at home, a jump that size is a recipe for a shoulder injury. 

Instead of trying to make a massive weight jump that your home gym kit can't support, we have a few ways to make those 24kg dumbbells feel heavy again. We can slow down the tempo to increase time under tension (like taking 3–4 seconds to lower the weight), add a pause at the chest, or increase the reps. 

Since your Dumbbell Bench Press today is programmed for 3x8 at 22.5kg per hand, you're actually very close to capping out your current dumbbells anyway. How many reps can you currently manage with the 24s before form starts to slip?

turns.user: so what do I actually do next week
turns.reply:
Next week we can keep the 24kg dumbbells in your hands but increase the target reps to 10 or 12 per set, or we can introduce a 3-second lowering phase on every single rep to make that weight feel significantly heavier. 

Another option is to swap the flat dumbbell bench press for a variation that is naturally harder, like a Dumbbell 1.5-Rep Bench Press or a decline press if you have an adjustable bench, which will make those 24s feel like plenty of weight. 

Which of those sounds like the best way to keep your chest working hard next week?
